name: Todd Wanek
current_role: President & CEO, Ashley Furniture Industries (Arcadia, Wisconsin)
profile: Son of founder Ron Wanek, Todd Wanek has been CEO of Ashley Furniture since 2002, after running its Taiwan factory for five years and becoming COO in 1996. Ashley is the world's largest home furnishings manufacturer and North America's largest furniture store brand; his father remains chairman.
interesting_fact: As a teen and college student he worked odd jobs at Ashley, including on the production line and shipping furniture, and after college spent five years living in Asia managing the company's Taiwan factory.
deep_cut_fact: He was named a 2026 Tampa Bay Father of the Year by the National Father's Day Council (June 2026 luncheon benefiting Big Brothers Big Sisters). Ashley's Hope to Dream program, which he describes as starting to help local kids who needed a mattress, passed 200,000 donated beds.

public_contacts.value: Sharon Okaah, Flytevu - sharon.okaah@flytevu.com (campaign media contact on Ashley press release)

notes: Best route is Ashley corporate PR (publicrelations@ashleyfurniture.com). Hope to Dream bed-donation program is a good warm hook. Flytevu contact appears campaign-specific.

name: Divyank Turakhia
current_role: Dubai-based tech entrepreneur and investor; founder and former CEO of Media.net, co-founder of Directi
profile: Mumbai-born programmer who co-founded web-hosting/domain group Directi with brother Bhavin in 1998 at age 16, then built contextual-ad network Media.net, sold in 2016 to a Chinese consortium for $900M, one of the largest ad-tech deals ever. Now based largely in Dubai, he invests and builds new ventures.
interesting_fact: He was named India's youngest billionaire three years running (2016-2018) and the youngest self-made Gulf billionaire in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He started coding at age eight; a 2021 interview with domain investor Mike Mann was titled 'From Wing Walking to Billion-Dollar Exits', and Entrepreneur India profiled his passion for flying planes and scuba diving.
notes: Low public profile; no verified personal social accounts or published office email found. Some web profiles about him are aggregator/AI-written; current title unverified. Don't confuse with brother Bhavin (Zeta, Flock).

name: Joan Tisch
profile: Died November 2, 2017 in Manhattan at age 90; widow of Preston Robert Tisch (Loews Corp. co-founder, NY Giants co-owner). Death announced by the New York Giants.
notes: Deceased (source: https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/joan-tisch-dead ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Tisch). Her stake passed to children Steve, Jonathan and Laurie Tisch. Remove from outreach list.

name: Akihiko Otsuka
profile: Former chairman of Otsuka Holdings and longtime president of Otsuka Pharmaceutical (1976-2000). Died November 28, 2014, aged 77, while serving as representative director and chairman, per Otsuka Holdings' official notice.
notes: Deceased (source: Otsuka Holdings TSE disclosure https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/45780/140120141201087645.pdf ; https://www.yakuji.co.jp/?p=40292). Current chairman is Ichiro Otsuka. Remove from outreach list.

name: Bradley Jacobs
current_role: Chairman & CEO, QXO (building products distribution); also to be chairman & CEO of new acquisition platform CKX
profile: Serial roll-up builder: United Waste (sold 1997 for $1.9B), United Rentals, then XPO Logistics (2011), which he split into XPO, GXO and RXO. Since 2024 he has run QXO, buying Beacon Roofing, Kodiak ($2.25B) and TopBuild (~$17B, closed July 2026), aiming for $50B revenue; in Nov 2026 he announced a second $1B-backed platform, CKX.
interesting_fact: A trained classical pianist, he studied math and music at Brown before dropping out; he has written two books, 'How to Make a Few Billion Dollars' (2024) and a 2025 sequel.
deep_cut_fact: His first company was Amerex Oil Associates, an oil brokerage he co-founded in 1979 and ran until its 1983 sale; he then moved to London and founded oil trader Hamilton Resources, and often credits financier Ludwig Jesselson as a mentor.
notes: Very media-friendly (books, frequent interviews). Best route: QXO media contact Joe Checkler. New CKX platform's target industry undisclosed - possible podcast hook.

name: Rajeev Juneja
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Mankind Pharma (New Delhi); President, PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (2025-26)
profile: Co-founded Mankind Pharma with elder brother Ramesh Juneja (company started 1991 with ~20 staff and INR 5M seed capital; incorporated 1995). Mankind sells affordable generics plus consumer brands (Manforce condoms, Prega News). He led its May 2023 IPO and the 2024 INR 13,630 crore acquisition of Bharat Serums and Vaccines.
interesting_fact: He and his younger brother were born on the same date, ten years apart; Amitabh Bachchan is Mankind's brand ambassador.
deep_cut_fact: He credits Mankind's growth to a 'startup culture' and the mantra of staying dynamic: 'In a fast-changing world, you cannot remain stationary... Every day is a new day.' He also said of the IPO: 'It makes you more responsible.'
notes: Also reachable via PHDCCI (industry chamber) in his presidency role. Company also lists investors@mankindpharma.com.

name: Alki David
current_role: Media/tech entrepreneur; founder of FilmOn and Hologram USA; shareholder in the Leventis-David group (Coca-Cola HBC)
profile: Lagos-born Cypriot-British heir to the Leventis-David trading family, whose holdings are tied to Coca-Cola HBC bottling. He founded internet-TV service FilmOn (2006), hologram-entertainment firm Hologram USA and other ventures, and acted in and directed independent films. No verified 2026 business activity found.
interesting_fact: He studied film at the Royal College of Art, acted in 'The Bank Job' (2008) and wrote/directed indie films such as 'Fishtales'.
deep_cut_fact: His father Andrew A. David joined the family's Leventis-David Group in Ghana in 1957 and managed a Coca-Cola bottling plant in Accra; in 1998 Alki co-founded London modelling agency Independent Models.
notes: HIGH REPUTATIONAL RISK: multiple civil sexual-misconduct judgments since 2019 (incl. a reported $900M jury award in 2024) and other legal issues per Wikipedia; in 2021 he called earlier billionaire claims 'complete fiction'. Journalist should vet carefully before any outreach. No published contact route found.

name: Henrik Mads Clausen
current_role: Shareholder of Danfoss A/S (no public executive or board role found)
profile: Born 1953, one of five children of Danfoss founder Mads Clausen and Bitten Clausen. He is listed as a direct owner of Danfoss alongside Clausen Controls A/S and the Bitten & Mads Clausen Foundation (largest shareholder). Danfoss, based in Nordborg, Denmark, makes drives, cooling, heating and power solutions, including for data centers.
interesting_fact: Danfoss was founded by his father Mads Clausen in 1933 in a farmhouse attic on the island of Als; the company now leads in energy-efficient cooling, drives and heat pumps.

public_contacts.value: lars.lohff@danfoss.com (Lars Grubak Lohff, Head of Media Relations, Danfoss)

notes: Very private; no public role. Family is represented on the Danfoss board by third-generation Mads Clausen and Mads-Peter Clausen - better interview targets for an energy/data-center podcast. Approach via Danfoss media relations.

name: Vichai Bencharongkul
profile: Member of Thailand's Bencharongkul telecom family behind Total Access Communication (dtac), founded 1989 and led by Boonchai Bencharongkul in partnership with Telenor; the family sold most of its dtac shares in 2005 and dtac merged into True Corporation in 2023. Could not verify Vichai's individual role or current status.

Benchachinda Holding is the likely family vehicle but its site blocked access. Verify identity and alive status before outreach.

name: Sebastian Glaser
current_role: Managing director of Sick Holding GmbH; majority shareholder of sensor maker SICK AG (Waldkirch, Germany)
profile: Grandson of optical engineer Erwin Sick, who founded SICK in 1946 near Munich; Glaser is the majority shareholder and runs the family's Sick Holding GmbH. SICK, led by external CEO Mats Gokstorp, makes industrial sensors, LiDAR and safety light curtains for factory, logistics and process automation, with ~10,000+ employees and >$2B sales.
interesting_fact: SICK laser scanners helped Stanford's autonomous car 'Stanley' win the 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge; the company's breakthrough was the first series-ready safety light curtain, shown at the Hannover fair in 1952.
notes: Low-profile family owner; operational spokespeople are SICK's executive board. Search budget ran out before a deep-cut fact or named press email could be sourced. Route via SICK corporate communications.

name: Satish Mehta
current_role: Founder, Managing Director & CEO, Emcure Pharmaceuticals (Pune)
profile: Son of a pharma distributor, Satish Mehta founded Emcure in Pune in 1981 as a contract manufacturer for multinationals, then moved into branded generics and biologics. Backed by Bain Capital, Emcure listed on NSE/BSE in July 2024 at a 31% premium; daughter Namita (Shark Tank India judge) and son Samit sit on the board.
interesting_fact: Emcure partnered with Roche (2012) to manufacture cancer drugs Herceptin and MabThera in India, and in 2013 launched a health-foods venture with cricketer MS Dhoni as brand ambassador.
deep_cut_fact: He started Emcure in 1981 with a bank loan of just Rs 3 lakh (about US$35,000 at the time).
notes: Emcure site blocked automated access, so no IR/press email captured; as a listed company it publishes an investor-relations contact on emcure.com and in stock-exchange filings - check manually. Daughter Namita Thapar is the family's most public face.

name: Sergei Gordeev
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~60%) of PIK Group, Russia's largest homebuilder; stepped down as CEO in 2022
profile: Moscow real-estate investor who made his fortune converting Soviet-era factories into offices (Rosbuilding, 1995; Horus Capital, sold 2010) and then took control of homebuilder PIK after buying a 20% stake from Suleiman Kerimov in 2013. He was PIK's CEO 2014-2022 and an early investor in Hyperloop One; he also served in Russia's Federation Council 2005-2010.
interesting_fact: He led the restoration of Moscow's constructivist Narkomfin building (Moisei Ginzburg, late 1920s), and his Stanislavsky Factory theatre-and-office conversion with John McAslan + Partners won a RIBA International Award (2011).
deep_cut_fact: In 2006 he bought the Melnikov House in Moscow and donated it to the state as a public museum; that year he also founded the Russian Avant-garde foundation, which has published 80+ books, and he gave his architectural graphics collection to the Schusev Museum of Architecture.
notes: Russia-based; check current sanctions/compliance position before any engagement (not verified here - search budget exhausted). Architecture and avant-garde preservation are his evident passions. No published personal contact found; PIK corporate IR is the only obvious route.

name: John Oyler
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, BeOne Medicines (formerly BeiGene; Nasdaq: ONC)
profile: Pittsburgh-raised MIT mechanical engineer and Stanford MBA who started at McKinsey, then founded Telephia (sold to Nielsen for $449M in 2007) and drug-discovery CRO BioDuro (sold to PPD). In 2010 he co-founded BeiGene with Chinese biochemist Xiaodong Wang; renamed BeOne, it is a global oncology company with ~11,000 staff, and he owns nearly 5%.
interesting_fact: BeOne's blood-cancer drug Brukinsa generated more than $2 billion in U.S. sales in 2024, and the company has 40+ drugs in its pipeline.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he was a mechanical engineer by training (MIT) and a McKinsey consultant; his first startup, Telephia, measured consumer mobile-phone usage, a far cry from oncology.
notes: Entrepreneurial serial founder story (telecom data -> CRO -> oncology) fits an entrepreneurship podcast. Best route: BeOne media relations (media@beonemed.com).

name: B. Wayne Hughes Jr
current_role: Founder, American Commercial Equities (real estate); founder of Serving USA and the Hughes Charitable Foundation (Jackson, Wyoming)
profile: Son of Public Storage co-founder B. Wayne Hughes (d. 2021), he worked at Public Storage from 1983 for nearly two decades (VP acquisitions 1992-2002) and sat on its board until late 2020. In 2005 he launched American Commercial Equities, which owns property in Hawaii and California; he now focuses largely on philanthropy from Wyoming.
interesting_fact: His Hughes Charitable Foundation focuses on education, at-risk youth, and food and housing insecurity in his home state of Wyoming; he is a USC graduate.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Serving USA, which funds Christ-centered nonprofits serving prisoners, women in recovery and military veterans, including prison-ministry and urban ministry training partners such as TUMI.
notes: Private; philanthropy (prison re-entry, veterans, Wyoming) is the warmest hook. Not an obvious energy/data-center guest.

name: Anurang Jain
current_role: Managing Director and majority owner, Endurance Technologies (Aurangabad/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, India)
profile: Nephew of the late Rahul Bajaj, Anurang Jain founded Endurance Technologies in 1985 to supply aluminium castings to Bajaj Auto. Endurance now makes suspension, braking, transmission and casting parts for two- and three-wheelers in India and car parts in Europe, with 18 plants in India and 9 in Europe.
interesting_fact: His twin brother Tarang Jain runs a rival auto-components group, Varroc Engineering; their father Naresh Chandra chaired both companies until retiring in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: His business philosophy, quoted on his Forbes profile: 'At Endurance, we believe that uncertainty is the new normal in business.'
notes: Endurance is NSE/BSE-listed and publishes an investor-relations contact on endurancegroup.com and in exchange filings, but the site blocked automated access - check manually. Search budget exhausted, so deep-cut fact is thin.

name: Alex Birkenstock
current_role: Private investor; former co-owner of Birkenstock (exited his remaining stake after the October 2023 IPO). Lives in Tegernsee, Germany.
profile: One of Karl Birkenstock's three sons, Alex took joint control of the family shoemaker in 2002, running his own brands under a multi-brand setup. He and brother Christian bought out brother Stephan in 2013 and sold a majority to L Catterton and Bernard Arnault's Financiere Agache in 2021 (>$4.5B), keeping minority stakes; Alex sold out after the 2023 NYSE IPO.
interesting_fact: The Birkenstock line traces to 1774 records of shoemaker Johannes Birkenstock in Hesse; his father Karl's 1963 'Original Birkenstock Footbed Sandal' (later the 'Madrid') was initially a commercial flop.
deep_cut_fact: His father Karl created, in 1962, the first standardized, permanently installed anatomical insole, which made healthy footwear mass-producible; earlier generations had made individually fitted insoles, and great-grandfather Konrad trademarked 'Fussbett' in 1925.
notes: Very private since exiting the company; no published personal contact or current venture found (search budget exhausted). Birkenstock corporate PR no longer represents him.

name: Oran Holtzman
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, Oddity Tech (Nasdaq: ODD)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who, with sister Shiran Holtzman-Erel (Chief Product Officer), bought the 1972 New York makeup brand Il Makiage and relaunched it as a digital-first business, forming Oddity Tech in 2018. Oddity uses AI/computer vision to match shoppers to products across Il Makiage, SpoiledChild and METHODIQ; it IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2023 at ~$2.7B and is HQ'd in New York with R&D in Tel Aviv.
interesting_fact: Oddity sells only online to 50M+ customers and runs its own biotech lab in Boston after acquiring AI molecular-discovery startup Revela in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Il Makiage was founded in 1972 by New York makeup artist Ilana Harkavi; L Catterton took a $29M minority stake in 2017, a year before the Holtzman siblings' digital relaunch.
notes: Data/AI-driven consumer company - good fit for an entrepreneurship/data podcast. Best route: press@oddity.com. Forbes lists him as UK-based.

name: Anne Graff
current_role: Likely minority shareholder of Graff Diamonds Corp. (no executive role found)
profile: Most likely Anne-Marie Graff (now credited as Anne-Marie Graff Ali), a French national who married jeweller Laurence Graff in 1962 and holds the stake in Graff Diamonds Corp. not owned by him (he holds ~60%). Graff, founded by Laurence in 1960, is run by their son Francois Graff as chief executive.
interesting_fact: Graff Diamonds has owned some of the world's most famous stones, including the Wittelsbach-Graff blue diamond (bought 2008) and the 302.37-carat Graff Lesedi La Rona, cut in 2019.
